questions.q: What order does Salesforce's own architecture guidance recommend for integration design decisions?
options: Choose the specific API technology first, then figure out what pattern it happens to support
Understand the integration pattern the need actually calls for first, then choose the Salesforce technology that implements it
There is no recommended order; both decisions are made simultaneously by convention
Choose the pattern and technology at random and test which one works
questions.explain: Starting with a technology question before understanding the actual pattern needed tends to produce a design that's technically functional but doesn't match how the business process really needs to behave — pattern should come first.

questions.q: What is the defining characteristic of a synchronous integration?
options: It never actually completes
The caller sends a request and waits for a response before continuing
It only works with batch jobs
It requires no network connection at all
questions.explain: A synchronous call blocks — the caller waits for the result before moving on — which is appropriate exactly when the calling process genuinely cannot proceed without that answer.

questions.q: Which pattern best describes Salesforce sending order details to an ERP system when an Opportunity is Closed Won, without waiting for the ERP to finish generating an invoice?
options: Request and Reply
Data Virtualization
Fire and Forget
Remote Call-In
questions.explain: Fire and Forget invokes a remote process without waiting for it to complete — Salesforce hands off the order details and the sales rep moves on, trusting the ERP to handle invoicing independently.

questions.q: What does Data Virtualization (e.g., via Salesforce Connect and external objects) avoid, compared to storing a copy of external data in Salesforce?
options: The need for any network connectivity at all
The need to keep two copies of the same data reconciled, since Salesforce reads the data live from the external system when needed
The need for any synchronous calls ever
The need for object-level security on external objects
questions.explain: Rather than copying and storing external data and having to keep it in sync with the source, data virtualization reads it live at the moment it's needed — at the cost of depending on the external system's availability whenever that data is viewed.

questions.q: How does this lesson connect Lesson 15's master data question to integration pattern choice?
options: It says the two decisions are completely unrelated

Once you know which system owns the truth for a piece of data, that answer directly shapes whether a synchronous (e.g., data virtualization) or asynchronous (e.g., batch sync) pattern makes sense for keeping Salesforce in sync with it
It says integration patterns always override master data decisions
It claims data architecture decisions are made entirely independently of any integration technology
questions.explain: If an external system owns a piece of data, whether Salesforce needs it in real time (favoring data virtualization) or can tolerate scheduled delay (favoring batch synchronization) is a direct consequence of the master data decision, not a separate, unrelated question.
